text:
Ava: Heads-up — running into duplicates in traces from the inference edge + backend path. Causing cost attribution to double-count some requests. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Matt: yep. common when the frontend generates a span and the backend re-emits with a new trace id. We end up with two ingestion records for same logical request.

Jordan: can we rely on a canonical request id passed through the call chain? e.g. `X-Redwood-Request-ID` header set by client and propagated. dedupe at ingest by that id.

Sana: +1 for canonical id but tricky: clients aren't always trusted — need to dedupe defensively. Also we have probes/retries that legitimately create new ids for retries.

Ava: thinking out loud: ingest dedupe strategy -> look up `canonical_request_id` in fast store (redis) with short TTL (30s). If seen, drop duplicate or merge metadata (tenant, route, token_count). Fallback if store unavailable: accept and mark `dedupe_status=unknown`.

Priya: tradeoffs: extra lookup per event adds RPS to redis and latency. At 10k rps that’s nontrivial. We could batch dedupe checks or do probabilistic bloom filter pre-check.

Matt: what about doing dedupe only for events that have cost_relevant=true? That reduces load because most spans are telemetry-only. Also prefer async dedupe in pipeline: accept everything, then dedupe in a downstream stage before cost aggregation.

Jordan: async dedupe has ordering problems. if we wait to dedupe, cost metrics may already be computed and exported. We'd need to make cost aggregation idempotent or support corrections. That's more plumbing.

Sana: alternative: canonicalization at the edge. Edge sets `X-Redwood-Request-ID` and signs it with `X-Redwood-Sig` HMAC. Backend verifies and copies it into span root. That prevents forged ids and means we can trust client header without remote lookup. Only cost is HMAC verify CPU.

Ava: love the signature idea — reduces redis dependency. But remember private deployments where we can't share keys; customers manage KMS. We'll need a per-customer signing key configuration + rotation.

Priya: if we do signature + short TTL local cache at ingest for replay protection, we can keep storage costs low. Also: store a small dedupe bitmap per tenant keyed by truncated hash to reduce memory.

Matt: ops question — if we dedupe, what's our canonical merge rule for tenant attribution when frontend and backend disagree? prefer backend if present, else frontend. Document fallback.

Jordan: agree. Also push: expose `dedupe_action` in event metadata (`accepted`, `merged`, `dropped`, `unknown`) so downstream teams can audit.

Ava: sounds like a path: (1) edge-signed `X-Redwood-Request-ID`, (2) ingest verify signature, (3) short local cache/bloom dedupe, (4) async repair job for missed/late duplicates. Will write RFC draft.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-8943: "dedupe + signed request id for inference pipeline" — https://tracker.redwood.internal/INF-8943

Sana: pinging infra owners for capacity calc — need expected additional qps on verification and cache.

Priya: I'll prototype a small Bloom filter vs redis cost comparison tomorrow.

Ava: thanks — I'll sketch the RFC with sequence diagrams and the merge rules. If anyone has objections or missing edge-cases, drop them here.

Matt: minor edge-case: SDK retries that happen within same client process — they reuse id already, so fine. But cross-process retries could produce new ids without signed reuse; consider hop-by-hop retry header.

Jordan: also mention sampling interplay: sampled traces may hide duplicates; we must ensure cost attribution uses unsampled telemetry or a companion low-sample stream for cost.

Ava: noted. I'll include a section: sampling + dedupe interaction and recommended config (sample for traces but send all cost markers).

Sana: thanks — super helpful.
